recommendations.recommendation:
Decision 12 should not turn on whether Anthropic is trustworthy. It should turn on whether this repository can say, afterwards and from evidence, what it sent. Today it cannot, and that is the whole of the objection to adding the secret.

The mechanism that closes the gap is small. A standard-library helper at `tools/egress/record.py` with a test at `tests/test_egress_record.py`, and three steps added to each of the two Claude workflows: a `check` before the call that fails the job when `docs/policies/egress.md` or the Decision 12 record is missing from the checkout or when the declared class exceeds what that workflow may send, the existing action step given an `id`, and a `write` after the call with `if: always()` that emits the seven fields of spec section 5 to the job summary and to an uploaded artifact. Both files were written and run before being proposed: nine tests, OK, exit 0. The order matters more than the code. The check runs first, so with no decision record in the tree the Claude step never executes. The record is a gate, not a log.

Three properties of the record are worth the owner's attention.

| Property | What it means |
|---|---|
| Exactly seven fields | `serialise` refuses any other field set, and a test asserts it, so the record cannot drift away from the spec sentence it implements |
| Secrets are excluded structurally, not filtered | The helper reads only an eight-name allowlist of `GITHUB_*` variables, so `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` are never read. A token-shape scan over the serialised line is the second layer. No pull request text, issue text, comment text or model output is copied in; sources appear only as hashes |
| A failed precondition writes a refused line, not no line | Once the call has happened, a missing record is worse than an admitted refusal |

The record lives in the job summary and in an artifact, and is rolled up into a committed `docs/runs/egress/index.jsonl` by a periodic pull request. The workflow must not commit it: `claude-review` holds only `contents: read`, the `pull_request` checkout is a merge ref that cannot be pushed, branch protection on `main` is Decision 6, and a push to the head branch would re-trigger the very workflow that made it. The cost is honest and must be named in the decision: artifacts default to 90 days, so between roll-ups the ledger is transient, and the roll-up is a standing human obligation with no mechanical trigger.

The ledger is read rather than merely written by tying it to three things that already exist: a fifth check in `tools/ci/checks.py`, which the `checks` job already runs on every pull request; a reconciliation run record in the format `docs/runs/2026-09-02-roadmap-revision-2/README.md` established, whose real work is comparing the ledger against the Actions run list so that a run which egressed without recording is visible; and the phase-exit criterion the operating model already uses at P2-2, extended to Phases 0 and 1 with Anthropic as the provider.

What the mechanism does not close, and what the decision record must say in its own voice: the ledger records what the run made available, not what the model read. The exact bytes are only in the action's `execution_file`, which the action's own documentation says may contain secrets, so it is neither kept nor hashed. For the `@claude` workflow the bound is looser still, because tag mode fetches comments and reviews through the API after the event payload was written. The data class is a declaration no script can verify. And the recorder lives inside the thing it records, so a pull request that deletes the record steps still runs `claude-review` from its own head. Only the owner's review of the diff covers that last one.

My recommendation: record Decision 12 and `docs/policies/egress.md` first, land this mechanism and the amendments to the operating model's section 8 table, the github-automation page, and the `CLAUDE.md` prohibition in the same pull request, and add the secret only after a run of `checks` proves the record steps are present. Then the first `claude-review` run leaves a record, and the sentence "every external submission records the seven fields" stops being a promise.
